AuthorizationVersion.description:
The one durable authorization-stream witness. The incarnation closes reset
and restore ABA; the JS-safe epoch advances for ordinary authorization
events within that stream.

@ref LLP 0053#the-authorization-version — v1 has one global durable pair.

IssuerId.description: A boot identity is never reused, even when process-local counters restart.

PublishedScopeRetirement.description:
Opaque evidence that a scope-retirement proof was released by the same
registry mutation that removed the covered live scope. The inner wire
record remains cloneable/deserializable for protocol inspection, but only
a successful registry commit can wrap it for a server publication.

@ref LLP 0303#s-a-compile-fail-witness-proves-a-spelling-is-gone-not-a-capability —
every client-visible retirement consumer requires this effect-bound
carrier, so reconstructing the public wire record does not recreate the
publication capability.

Receipt.description:
A retention-ring receipt (LLP 0034 §3.2): connectionless facts about
mutations and subscription lifecycle, served by the receipts snapshot and
echoed in live-subscribe/unsubscribe outputs. Privacy (§3.3): receipts
carry opaque ids, versions, table names, and reasons — never row data or
argument values.

oneOf.description:
One mutation invocation: confirmed or rejected, with the write
surface that fan-out used.

affectedTables.description:
`null` means EXPLICITLY unknown (an IbexModule handler without a
declared write set) — distinct from `[]`, no tables.

claimLedger.description:
Private settlement evidence. `None` is the fan-out projection;
the submitting authority's direct response always carries `Some`.

enqueues.description:
Jobs this confirmed mutation durably enqueued in its own
transaction (LLP 0070 first slice; 0127 decision 7's
mutation-side association). Bounded facts only — jobId, action,
availableAtMs; never argument values. Omitted when empty, and a
rejected mutation never carries one: the receipt proves what was
scheduled with the write, and its absence on a rejection is the
inspectable rollback-schedules-nothing evidence.

idMap.description:
Private lane-L id reconciliation. `Some([])` is the explicit
no-mints map; `None` means this is lane Q or a fan-out projection.

rollbackReason.description:
The diagnostic CODE only — messages may embed argument values
(§3.3 privacy). `null` on confirmed mutations.

sequenceAllocations.description:
Private sequence evidence for the submitting authority. The value
discloses prior allocation count, so fan-out projection strips it.
@ref LLP 0135#17-allocation-authority-and-information-flow — effect
  receipts carry the full counter/scope/incarnation/value tuple
  only on the submitter's receipt.

settlementLane.description: Server-observed settlement policy. Safe to retain in fan-out.

snapshotVersion.description:
`null` only when the rejected invocation could not safely read the
durable cursor; never fabricate zero from a storage failure.

oneOf.description:
Subscription lifecycle: established / disposed, on both the durable
live-query lane and the ephemeral room lane (`lane: "ephemeral"`,
which carries `bindingId`/`collection` instead of `subscriptionId`).

snapshotVersion.description:
`null` when no storage read is safe at the emission site (the
disconnect teardown path) — the honest "unknown at death" value.

ScopeRetirement.description:
Server-authenticated proof that one current-issuer namespace has no live or
unresolved scope at or below a contiguous scope-sequence prefix. The proof
is a cleanup/fencing fact only; accepting it never stands in for a result
snapshot, a resolution ACK, or a release proof.

SequenceAllocationFact.description:
One tentative sequence value. It is returned during handler execution but
becomes a fact only if this exact identity/value transition commits.

@ref LLP 0135#13-allocation-versus-commit-ordering-and-gap-semantics — the
  counter advance is buffered and commits or rolls back with app writes.

SettlementClaimDisposition.description:
How settlement treated one client-captured application value. Divergence
remains visible in the claimed/authoritative pair rather than becoming a
fourth disposition.

@ref LLP 0133#receipts — settlement receipts carry labeled claims, while
  fan-out projections omit their values entirely.

SettlementLane.description:
Settle-time trust policy selected by an ordinary client-attested mutation
label. The default preserves the pre-0133 queued replay contract for older
request and retained-artifact decoders.

@ref LLP 0133#the-two-settlement-lanes — the label selects replay acceptance
  or server re-derivation without granting authority.
